houseViews.view: Strong but the headline overstates it. SA shows ~28% 1-yr sold $/m2 growth, but one new premium estate (Riverlea Park) is ~34% of 2026 sales; excluding it growth is ~18%, and like-for-like across matched suburbs ~9.5%. Real, supply-tight growth (stock ~6 months vs ~13 national) with composition inflating the optics.
houseViews.falsifier: Two consecutive months of rising inflow or incentive share, or like-for-like growth converging to zero.

houseViews.view: The affordability ceiling is the central SA risk: package-to-income multiple is now among the worst in the nation (see affordability table) despite SA historically being the cheap state. Supply scarcity currently outweighs it, so expect deceleration toward single-digit growth rather than correction while stock stays under ~7 months.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months or sold rates softening two runs in a row.

houseViews.view: Archetypal rocketship late-stage: $/m2 tripled in 3 years while lots compressed ~47% to defend price points. Compression that deep usually precedes a plateau ??? sellers of stage stock are better placed than buyers of englobo at current rates.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m2 keeps rising on solid volume.

houseViews.view: Genuine fallen-angel territory: Bendigo sold rates are down ~36-38% from peak with lot sizes re-expanding ??? the classic cannot-hold-the-rate signal. The contrarian question is timing: falls followed strong growth and regional VIC fundamentals (population, infrastructure) remain, so this reads temporal-leaning, but confirm two quarters of stabilising sold rates before buying conviction.
houseViews.falsifier: A third consecutive falling year or inflow collapse.

houseViews.view: Asking is running ~50%+ above certified sold ($/m2) ??? vendor ambition meets a genuinely tightening market (Gifford Hill 17,100-home project will anchor long-run supply). Near-term: negotiation window on acquisitions; releases must price to clear, not to comps.
houseViews.falsifier: New sales landing at or above current asking rates.
